subject: social
title: North Carolina Places
about: North Carolina's three regions (mountains in the west, piedmont in the middle, coastal plain in the east), the Outer Banks, the Appalachian and Blue Ridge Mountains, Charlotte as the biggest city, and the four neighbor states. NC 1.G.1.1: use maps to identify places and landforms.
tip: Open a North Carolina map and have him point to the mountains, the piedmont and the coast, then to where you live.

cards.q: North Carolina is split into three big land areas. What are those areas called?
cards.note: The three regions are the mountains, the piedmont and the coastal plain.

cards.q: Which North Carolina region has the tallest land?
cards.note: The mountain region is in the west.

cards.q: The middle region of North Carolina, with rolling hills, is called the...
cards.note: Most people in North Carolina live in the piedmont.

cards.q: The flat region of North Carolina next to the ocean is called the...
cards.note: The coastal plain is in the east, by the Atlantic Ocean.

cards.q: The word piedmont means foot of the...
cards.note: The piedmont sits at the foot of the mountains.

cards.q: From the piedmont, which direction do you drive to reach the ocean?
cards.note: The beach is east. The sun comes up over the ocean there.

cards.q: From the piedmont, which direction do you drive to reach the mountains?
cards.note: The mountains are west. The sun sets behind them.

cards.q: Raleigh, the state capital, is in which region of North Carolina?
cards.note: Raleigh and Charlotte are both in the piedmont.

cards.q: What is the biggest city in North Carolina?
cards.note: Charlotte has the most people. Raleigh is the capital.

cards.q: The long, thin islands along North Carolina's coast are called the...
cards.note: The Outer Banks have beaches, wild horses and the Kitty Hawk flight spot.

cards.q: On the Outer Banks, what tall tower with a bright light helps ships stay safe?
cards.note: The Cape Hatteras Lighthouse is on the Outer Banks. It has black and white stripes.

cards.q: North Carolina's mountains are part of a long mountain chain called the...
cards.note: The Appalachian Mountains run through many states.

cards.q: Some North Carolina mountains look blue from far away. They are called the...
cards.note: A soft blue haze hangs over the Blue Ridge Mountains.

cards.q: Which is bigger: North Carolina or the United States?
cards.note: North Carolina is one of the 50 states inside the United States.

cards.q: Which state is to the west of North Carolina, past the mountains?
cards.note: Tennessee is on the other side of the mountains.

cards.q: North Carolina touches four states: Virginia, South Carolina, Tennessee and...
cards.note: Georgia touches the bottom left corner of North Carolina.

cards.q: How many states touch North Carolina?
cards.note: Virginia, South Carolina, Georgia and Tennessee.

cards.q: The coastal plain has flat land and good soil. What do many people there do?
cards.note: Sweet potatoes and many other crops grow on the coastal plain.
